In the 11 years it was open, Everson Royce Bar appealed to casual and knowledgeable drinkers alike, serving as a watering hole […]
items.text: LA Restaurant Closings With LA’s Bar Scene in Crisis, Everson Royce Bar Announces Last Call Co-owner Randy Clement says tourism is down, costs are up, and the entertainment workforce is staying home﻿ by Mona Holmes Nov 4, 2026, 11:51 PM UTC Facebook Link Everson Royce Bar in Arts District. Wonho Frank Lee Mona Holmes is an editor at Eater Southern California/Southwest, a regular contributor at KCRW radio, and a 2022 James Beard Award nominee. In late October, Downtown’s Everson Royce Bar announced it would close permanently at the end of 2026. Hundreds of comments on its Instagram page lamented the loss of another fundamental Los Angeles bar. In the 11 years it was open, Everson Royce Bar appealed to casual and knowledgeable drinkers alike, serving as a watering hole for the hospitality industry. Cocktail culture writer Esther Tseng recalls the bar’s impact on the region. “It’s a bar that always had seriously good (but not serious) cocktails,” says Tseng. “It was probably one of the first places I knew Downtown that could accommodate small parties in an intimate bar setting, or larger, casual parties on the patio out back. It had great food, too.” Partners Joe Capella, Randy Clement, April Langford, and chef Matt Molina debuted Everson Royce Bar in 2015 with an uncomplicated approach to cocktails, a selection of rare whiskeys, Molina’s notable cheeseburger and food menu , plus that welcoming outdoor area. The team brought plenty of experience from restaurants and bars across Southern California. Capella and Molina are longtime operators of Hippo and South Pasadena’s Cannonball , which opened in 2025. Wife-and-husband team Langford and Clement are the minds behind Good Neighbor Bar as well as West Altadena Wine, which the couple closed in October. Eater spoke to Clement about the reasoning behind his decision to shutter Everson Royce Bar and West Altadena Wine. Clement cited the same challenges other operators have in Los Angeles’s current business and consumer climate : a significant drop in tourism, rising operational costs, changing drinking trends, plus the long-term effects of the pandemic and entertainment industry strikes. This year has been one of the hardest for Southern California bars and nightlife. Clement sees businesses losing their customer base as the many film and television workers who have long fueled Los Angeles restaurants and bars — hospitality workers pursuing entertainment dreams with side gigs as well as higher-paid industry professionals — can no longer afford to go out to eat and drink regularly. “Closing Everson Royce was the perfect storm of everything going wrong at the same time,” says Clement. “But unless there is this other unnamed industry waiting in the wings to replace the industry that’s driven our town for the last decades upon decades, I’m concerned that there’s no looking back.” The foursome saw the numbers and had acknowledged the inevitable for some time. They extended the closure announcement to keep their workers employed, with a persistent optimism that conditions would improve. As for West Altadena Wine, which is attached to Good Neighbor Bar’s patio, Clement says he was unwilling to continue the lengthy conflict with a residential neighbor who allegedly targeted the business by complaining to government agencies like Los Angeles County’s Department of Public Works, Building and Safety, LA County Planning, and the Department of Public Health. Clement also says that the complainant called law enforcement before Langford and Clement finally closed West Altadena Wine in late October. Eater reached out to the complainant but did not hear back. Clement and Langford moved from Albuquerque, New Mexico, to Los Angeles in 1996. The couple currently resides in Altadena and, along with other Los Angeles operators, worries about business sustainability and the city’s culture. “Here in LA, anything is possible, and now it doesn’t feel like that,” says Clement. The year 2026 is proving challenging for Los Angeles nightlife. West Hollywood’s the Belmont shuttered in August, and the neighborhood’s renowned Employees Only closed in late September. On November 2, Augustine Wine Bar announced it will close on December 19, the same day as Everson Royce Bar. SF Gate reports that cocktail (and wings) favorite Ye Rustic Inn might lose its outdoor seating and cites lease concerns with the landlord. Owner Susan Wood hosted an event to bolster support for the almost 30-year-old bar, where Los Angeles mayoral candidate and councilmember Nithya Raman showed up to offer support for independent businesses. (As of this writing, one day after Election Day, Raman holds a small lead over incumbent Mayor Karen Bass.) Clement sees an emergency unfolding and hopes solutions can come from elected officials for all independent businesses. “If you’re the group formulating legislation for economic incentives or tax credits, the fact that this hasn’t happened yet, maybe it’s all too late,” says Clement. “I don’t know. What Everson Royce Bar is going through is what the florist, yoga studio, and bookstore are going through.” Everson Royce Bar Everson Royce Bar 1936 E 7th St, Los Angeles, CA, 90021, US Booking Book a table Phone (213) 335-6166 Link http://www.erbla.com/ See More : LA Restaurant Closings LA Restaurant News Cocktail Bars Most Popular The Best Restaurants in Palm Springs, According to Eater Editors The Best Los Angeles Restaurants for Thanksgiving Dinner The 18 Best Santa Monica Restaurants The 21 Best Indian and South Asian Restaurants in Los Angeles The Best Restaurants in Downtown Los Angeles, According to Eater Editors Advertiser Content From This is the title for the native ad

With award-winning drinking dens found all over town, it’s easier than ever to get your hands on a delicious cocktail in Miami right now. With that in mind, below is an updated list of Miami’s go-to cocktail spots to grab a well-balanced drink. This list only includes cocktail bars in the most traditional sense (i.e., ones that are more focused on drink than food — and doesn’t include breweries , wine bars , or restaurants with really, really great bar programs ) and have been open for around six months or longer. From an iconic pina colada on South Beach to the best happy hour , these spots know the classics, while also keeping up with fun drinking trends like the rise of the tiny tini (hello, Sweet Liberty) and creating a fun atmosphere that makes you want to stick around for a while. Elcielo Elcielo received a Michelin Star for its 18-course tasting menu by chef Juan Manuel Barrientos. The tasting menu ranges from $245 to $289 per person (excluding beverages, tax, and a 20 percent added gratuity). Elcielo will accommodate people with allergies and offer a vegetarian menu upon request. items.text: Tin Tin Dining Out in Miami The Best New Bars in Miami Where to grab a drink right now in the Magic City by Allison Ramirez Updated Jul 15, 2026, 1:00 PM UTC Facebook Link Allison Ramirez is a freelance journalist with over 15 years of experience covering food and drink, travel, art, culture, and more. As a gateway between the U.S., the Caribbean, and Latin America, Miami has long been a champion of diverse flavors — rum and agave spirits mingling with notes of citrus and exotic fruits. Recently, vermouth and sherry-based drinks, along with classic Spanish cocktails and Italian spritzes, are popping up in the local scene, further shaping the city’s evolving cocktail landscape. Miami’s drinking culture really reflects its melting pot history, and this year, some iconic bars and restaurants have reopened with a refreshed look and feel, bringing back old-school favorites alongside international, travel-inspired drinks. From tiki recipes and passion fruit infusions to sparkling concoctions of all sorts, our latest cocktail map highlights the best drinks and the hottest new spots to try them, from Coral Gables to Miami Beach and everywhere in between. Sunny’s Steakhouse Sunny’s Steakhouse in Miami’s Little River has been the talk of the town (many towns, actually) since opening in October 2024. The massive space and the dishes are worth the hype, but the unspoken star is the bar, featuring cocktails like the refreshing Green Ghoul (tequila, mezcal, poblano, cucumber, lime) and the Monchito, a coconut-washed agricole rhum drink with sherry that evolved from a piña colada to a ti punch of sorts. The menu includes house cocktails, martinis, and “fine & fancy” options — the fino martini service, which comes with a sidecar, is a must. Made with gin, clarified passionfruit, and fino sherry, it’s a steal at $18 per person. Try a low ABV Red Foulard made with Savoia (an all-natural orange wine aperitivo), Select Aperitivo (a Venetian bittersweet orange liqueur), and soda; or go bold with spirit-forward, aperitif-driven gin cocktails like the Signora del Lago (22% ABV) or Martini Catalano (25% ABV). items.summary: A new Mexican seafood restaurant, Mi Vecino, is opening in Circle C, courtesy of chef Amir Hajimaleki and his brother Ali Hajimaleki of Roya Hospitality Group. It’s slated to open between now and early 2027, per a release. The restaurant, Mi Vecino, will open at 5701 West Slaughter Lane, replacing another of the group’s restaurants, […]
items.text: Austin Restaurant News Fire-Grilled Mexican Seafood Is Coming to South Austin The team behind Roya and Oasthouse will open Mi Vecino, a coastal restaurant focused on raw and fire-kissed dishes by Erin Russell Oct 28, 2026, 6:47 PM UTC Facebook Link Chef Amir Hajimaleki will oversee the menu, managed by Mi Vecino’s executive chef Jose Alajandro Sanchez. Sarah Natsumi Moore/Eater Erin Russell is a journalist and an Austin native, who has been writing about food for eight years. A new Mexican seafood restaurant, Mi Vecino, is opening in Circle C, courtesy of chef Amir Hajimaleki and his brother Ali Hajimaleki of Roya Hospitality Group. It’s slated to open between now and early 2027, per a release. The restaurant, Mi Vecino, will open at 5701 West Slaughter Lane, replacing another of the group’s restaurants, Keeper’s Coastal Kitchen , which closed Saturday, October 24. Mi Vecino, which means my neighbor in Spanish, will focus on Mexican seafood dishes, both raw and fire-grilled. That means offerings like shrimp enchiladas with white mole, ceviche, oysters, and fajitas served with fresh tortillas. Drinks-wise, there will be a full bar with margaritas, ranch waters, palomas, and other cocktails. Chef Hajimaleki will oversee the menu, which will be executed by chef Jose Alajandro Sanchez. The Hajimalekis’ restaurants are mostly clustered on Slaughter Lane in South Austin. Gastropub Oasthouse Kitchen + Bar , cocktail bar Daisy Lounge , and forthcoming Mi Vecino all share a building, and the group’s first restaurant , American spot District Kitchen + Cocktails , is just down the street. Mi Vecino replaces Keeper’s Coastal Kitchen, a different Roya Hospitality Group restaurant that closed in October. Jasmin Porter Photography This is not the first time Roya Hospitality Group has reimagined one of their restaurants. Roya , Hajimalekis’ highly personal Persian restaurant in North Shoal Creek, opened this year in a space that was previously Shortie’s, the group’s foray into New England Greek-style pizza. Roya is the group’s only North Austin restaurant, and sits above a former second District Kitchen, which closed and became an event space. Given the group’s penchant for reinvention, only time will tell whether it stays an event space. items.text: Fonda San Miguel Dining Out in Austin The Best Restaurants in Austin for Private Dining, Events, and Parties Everywhere to book for all of your small weddings, celebratory dinners, bridal showers, and more by Darcie Duttweiler Updated Oct 22, 2026, 2:00 PM UTC Facebook Link Darcie Duttweiler is an Austin-based freelance writer, who covers food, beverages, travel, and lifestyle. Whether you’re planning a milestone birthday, hosting a corporate dinner, or gathering friends for an engagement celebration, Austin has a private dining room to suit your needs. Some are swanky and tucked into Downtown dining landmarks. Others are cozy, or perched on patios with sweeping views. All of them make an outing feel like an event, while also taking the stress out of group dining — meaning, there’s no awkward table shuffling, no shouting over the crowd, and no fighting for the check. The city’s best private dining spaces are more than just a curtain and a prix fixe menu. Many spots go beyond dinner, offering perks like custom cocktails, floral design, built-in audio and video setups, and after-hours buyouts. From iconic institutions like Fonda San Miguel, Matties, and Jeffrey’s to sleek hotspots like Eberly, La Condessa, and Bar Toti, these venues combine atmosphere with standout service and memorable menus. Here are the city’s most impressive private and semi-private dining options — spaces that strike the right balance between style and function. In this update, the Peacock’s private dining room joins the map, and Prelude, Maie Day, and Bar Peached leave the list. items.title: Cotoletta’s Only Entree Honors Italian Traditions and Age-Old Techniques
items.summary:
At Cotoletta in Coconut Grove, there are no decisions to make. The Miami restaurant serves only one entree: Cotoletta alla… 
 The post  Cotoletta’s Only Entree Honors Italian Traditions and Age-Old Techniques  appeared first on  Resy | Right This Way .
items.text: Cotoletta’s Only Entree Honors Italian Traditions and Age-Old Techniques — Resy | Right This Way Cotoletta 4.7 · Italian · $ Miami Book Now Published: Nov. 9, 2026 At Cotoletta in Coconut Grove, there are no decisions to make. The Miami restaurant serves only one entree: Cotoletta alla Milanese. No substitutions. No alternatives. Just a golden, pan-fried veal cutlet — and a bet that it’s all you’ll need. Until recently, making a reservation required a phone call, which only deepened the sense that this place operates on its own terms. (The good news: You can now reserve a table on Resy.) The concept debuted in Coconut Grove in the fall of 2024 and comes from 84 Magic Hospitality, a restaurant group known for a growing collection of Miami restaurants with minimalist menus ( San Lorenzo , San Marco , and the lasagna speakeasy, Si Papa 3190 , are the others). Photo courtesy of Cotoletta Photo courtesy of Cotoletta Still, the story behind the concept stretches back further than its Miami address might suggest. Cotoletta is the creation of partners Ignacio Lopez Mancisidor and Mattia Cicognani, and former co-founder Andrea Fraquelli — who share a background in hospitality and a frustration with how transactional the industry had become. From the start, their goal at Cotoletta has been to make things simple for guests and allow them to focus on what really matters: great food and genuine connection. “Across the globe, many of the best restaurants do one item and they do it to absolute perfection,” co-founder Mattia Cicognani says. “We drew inspiration from the Italian essence of committing to one hero dish and prioritizing ingredients of the highest quality.” “Only serving one dish was a risk,” Cicognani acknowledges, “but the popularity and love for the concept has proven that it really works. Our customers learned that they love what we do and that is why they continue to come back.” Photo courtesy of Cotoletta Photo courtesy of Cotoletta Head chef Davide Rosselli shared the process that delivers a consistent, classic cotoletta every time. Premium veal is hand-trimmed, gently pounded to its thin-yet-tender texture, coated in fresh egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in clarified butter until it emerges with a crisp, even, golden crust. Each cutlet weighs in at roughly 20 ounces, made to be shared between two people. The result is a traditional veal Milanese that is a signature of Northern Italian craftsmanship. Everything else on the table exists to support that centerpiece. “While the process sounds simple, it’s backed by decades of Italian tradition and time-honored techniques passed down by chefs across generations,” Rosselli says. For $90, two diners share the full prix-fixe experience: two antipasti courses of bruschetta and truffle arancino to start, followed by the veal cutlet, and two sides (the only real choice you have to make here). Dessert (tiramisu or a flourless chocolate cake) can be added on for $14. “Each appetizer sets the tone for a true Italian experience, while the sides are thoughtfully chosen to complement the veal without overpowering it.” Rosselli says. “Lighter elements like crisp salads and simple pasta dishes help balance the richness of the veal, creating a well-rounded meal.” Those side options include pasta al pomodoro, zucchine fritte, insalata di rucola, or patatine fritte. Rosselli’s personal picks: the pasta in just the right portion to leave you wanting more of the main event, and the zucchine fritte offering a warm, light bite that balances out the richness of the veal. (Wondering what happens if you bring a third wheel or want to dine solo? Odd-numbered parties can add on an individual portion of bruschetta, arancino, a smaller veal cutlet, and one side for $55.) Guests return because the menu never changes, and neither does the reason to go back. “They know exactly what they are getting every single time,” Cicognani says. Cotoletta is open weekdays from 5:30 to 10 p.m. and until 10:30 p.m. on Friday. On weekends, it opens at 12:30 p.m. until 10:30 p.m. on Saturday and 9 p.m. on Sunday. Lyssa Goldberg is a Miami-based freelance writer and content strategist. She loves telling stories about food, wellness and travel, and you can find her byline in Parade, American Way, Mashable, Miami New Times, Time Out and more. Follow her on Instagram and Twitter . Follow Resy , too. items.text: Titán Dumbo Photo courtesy of Titán Tepporocho While we’re still mourning the loss of Leyenda, the arrival of Titán is more than getting us through. items.text: The Resy Guide to Bars and Restaurants for Music Lovers in New York — Resy | Right This Way Updated: Nov. 9, 2026 As people who love restaurants, we know that when it comes to picking a spot for dinner, it’s much more than about just the food. The vibe is just as important, and music is a key player in creating it. Sometimes, the best soundtrack is the one you don’t notice, but the places on this list aren’t for those kinds of nights. These playlists are hyper specific, the sound systems are top of the line, and often they have some of the best vinyl collections in the country, and a guest DJs on weekends who comes in to spin them. These are places you go to for the music, but where us restaurant lovers won’t need to suffer because the snacks that can often lead to full meals are far more interesting than a bag of stale potato chips. You’ll be able to listen to some Japanese jazz deep cuts over an omakase, or eclectic world beats over some of the city’s silkiest hummus — with playlists and menus like these, you might not need to make it to your second destination for the night. And if you’re looking for spots with live music, we’ve got you covered here . City Photo courtesy of 56709 What was once 929, an audio haven for Canto pop, is now a moody, atmospheric spot for Japanese city pop, from the same team. You’ll also find plenty of records that include J-pop from the 90s and 2000s, plus Japanese R&B. And the theme isn’t strictly limited to the music, either. Cocktails are named after Japanese pop stars (Anri, Momoko, Ryuichi) and anime (Agumon, Usagi), and food is a fusion of Japanese and Taiwanese flavors: Think radish cakes with XO sauce, braised pork over rice, and mala-seasoned French fries. Book Now Birds map West Village Whether you’re partial to live music or listening bar vibes, Birds has you covered. On weeknights they spin selections from their enormous vinyl collection, and on weekends they host live musicians in a variety of styles like ska, jazz, and Afrobeats. Know that on Fridays and Saturdays there’s a $30 cover charge, but it’s a small price to pay for the incredible night of music that you’re in for. Book Now Boro Brine map Williamsburg The bar. Photo by Ben Hon, courtesy of Boro Brine There are two concepts at this Williamsburg restaurant, an intimate 22-seat omakase counter and a Japanese-inspired cocktail bar. Audiophiles will be satisfied at either, as music runs throughout and the sound system is top notch. The chef’s tasting consists of an ever-changing menu of multiple courses for $98 a person, whereas the bar has an à la carte menu that features inventive cocktails and bites like a chef’s take on a filet-o-fish and octopus with saag paneer. With velvet banquets and a dimly lit interior, it’s also a perfect date night spot. Book Now ALL BLUES map Tribeca Photo courtesy of All Blues Don’t be surprised if you’re asked to keep quiet at this Tribeca listening room. It’s all about the music here, so much so to that conversation is discouraged. All Blues comes from owner Yuji Fukushima, who based the concept on the places he frequented back growing up in Tokyo. He’s invested in top-tier audio equipment and carefully selects the music each evening, which can range from funk to Dizzy Gillespie. Enjoy Japanese snacks like tempura sweet potatoes and gyoza, alongside a fine whiskey or sake while you take in the sounds. Book Now Record Room map Long Island City Photo courtesy of Record Room This Long Island City bar might be a little hard to find at first, but that’s the idea. Behind a hidden door, you’ll be transported to a music filled living room of sorts, filled with comfy couches and soft lighting. All the music here is played off vinyl and there might be occasional dancing. The drinks lean classic, with riffs on espresso martinis

items.text: 29 New York Bars and Restaurants with Excellent Zero-Proof Cocktails — Resy | Right This Way Updated: Nov. 9, 2026 Somewhere around a decade ago the dreaded term “mocktail” first started to surface on menus, referring to drinks meant to offer the cocktail experience, but none of the “buzz.” At the time, unlike their alcoholic counterparts, most of these drinks were overly sweet mixes of juice and housemade sodas with elaborate garnishes. Now, however, there’s been a shift in drinking culture: Dry January, anyone? In other words, we’re drinking less, or thinking about having that second or third drink more, and beverage directors have taken note. Today’s mocktails are now as considered and thoughtfully developed as those made full-strength. Many of them also feature the new wave of non-alcoholic spirits, like Seedlip, Lyre’s, Little Saints, Amass Riverine, and Ghia. So, whether you’re abstaining from alcohol, are taking a night off, or just want to stay and linger at the bar after your glass has run dry, here are some of the best places in the city to find zero-proof cocktails. Party Size Remove 2 Add Update Close Date Soft Bar + Cafe map Greenpoint One of the newer additions to the non-alcoholic cocktail scene in our fair city, Soft Bar is so named because all of the drinks on their all-day menu are, well, soft. The Golden Hour , with grape, elderflower, pink peppercorn shrub, and alcohol-free Champagne, or the Pear Pressure with prickly pear, agave, and alcohol-free Tequila, are both good choices. Keep an eye out on the menu for the function of each drink, which ranges from focus to “vibey.” Plus, there’s a celebrity at the helm – fans of Bravo’s Summer House might see a familiar face. Read all about Soft Bar here . Book Now Golden Ratio map Clinton Hill What can’t this team do? Golden Ratio comes from the masterminds behind Cafe Mado and Place des Fêtes , serving up cocktails and mocktails to the Clinton Hill crowd. Nearly all of the cocktails here have a nonalcoholic counterpart, and everything is fiercely flavor-driven and seasonal. Past drinks have included interpretations of purple shiso , apple , and toothache tree , and the team is working towards being zero-waste, so you can have your drink and eat it, too. Book Now Lord's map NoHo This beloved purveyor of British fare may not be the first thing that comes to mind when you think of nonalcoholic beverages, but their list (which they title “Teetotaling”) is one of our favorites. Go for a Blood Orange Spritz , a sour made with Ghia, or a S affron White Negroni — all totally alcohol free, of course. Any of them pairs perfectly with a good lamb Scotch egg, too. Book Now Sofreh map Prospect Heights There’s not a lot we’d say no to at Sofreh. While yes, their list of cocktails is excellent, the real pearl here has to be the selection of sharbats , a Persian cooler that comes in flavors like mint and cucumber, sour cherry, and lemon and saffron. If those aren’t doing it for you, there’s also the Persian black tea and a mint and rose petal yogurt drink. No matter what’s in your glass, make sure an order of herb meatballs and saffron rice are on your table. Book Now The Up & Up map Greenwich Village This subterranean cocktail den and ideal date night spot in Greenwich Village has an extensive list of drinks that also includes five excellent nonalcoholic takes on some of their classics. This includes a zero-proof spin of Hold, Please , a watermelon shrub that draws inspiration from New York’s sliced fruit vendors who often sell servings of watermelon spears topped with Tajín. There’s also an N/A version of Zuzu’s Petals , named for the classic film, “It’s a Wonderful Life,” that’s made with ginger, habanero, rose water, lime juice, and demerara. Book Now Spygold map Hudson Yards Greywind’s (also on this list) sister and downstairs neighbor, the fire-lit Spygold, has an equally lovely list of non-alcoholic options for you to peruse. Past favorites have included the Tomato, Tomahto with nonalcoholic gin and tomato-basil soda, or the Cucumber Highball with alcohol-free Tequila and cucumber soda. items.text: Amazonico Miami map Brickell Come dressed for dinner and whatever follows at Amazónico, where live bands play jazz, bossa nova, and Cuban rhythms beneath a canopy of greenery. The menu is as extravagant as the setting: guacamole comes topped with sea urchin, and Maine lobster tail arrives with semolina pasta and coconut bisque. Share ceviche with sweet plantain and duck arroz chaufa before moving on to charcoal-grilled picanha or Australian wagyu ribeye. items.title: 9 All-Inclusive Resorts in Cancún That Go Way Beyond an Open Bar
items.summary: From butler-serviced suites to sommelier-led tastings, these Mexico stays are redefining all-inclusive luxury.
items.text: North America Chevron Mexico Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story I first arrived in Cancún, Mexico , more than 20 years ago. I had big hair, pencil-thin eyebrows, and limited expectations for an all-inclusive vacation : A swim-up bar serving frozen margaritas was about all I needed. Since then, my priorities have shifted, and thankfully, Cancún’s all-inclusive resorts have grown up alongside me. After two decades of return visits made easier by an abundance of nonstop US flights , I’ve become more discerning about what deserves a place in that up-front price. I’ve also discovered that Cancún’s enduring spring break reputation tells an incomplete story about what's on offer. Choose the right resort, and you can have a butler draw your evening bath, a private pool overlooking the Caribbean, and à la carte restaurants you’ll look forward to all afternoon, whether you prefer the Hotel Zone’s long sweep of white sand, the relative quiet of Playa Mujeres, or a boat ride out to Isla Mujeres . The frozen margaritas are still here. But now, there’s much more worth checking in for. Read on for the best all-inclusive resorts in Cancún worth planning a vacation around. Rubén Soto’s concrete mural depicts native wildlife amid geometric patterns, while suites carry the aesthetic through warm woods and marble rather than tropical clichés. At Atelier, which welcomes ages 16+, you might have lunch overlooking the water at El Suspiro, then enjoy a pre-dinner mezcal cocktail at Bar de la Calle. Back in your suite, a rolling minibar holds wine and gourmet snacks, and room service answers around the clock. Most dining and premium spirits are included, though María Dolores by Edgar Núñez warrants a separate reservation—and budget—for its contemporary Mexican menu. Book an Inspira suite, and a butler can arrange your dinner reservations while you spend the afternoon at the rooftop infinity pool. Once you’re settled, the day’s agenda might amount to a poolside cocktail, a soak in the spa’s hydrotherapy pools, and deciding what to wear to dinner. This adults-only Hotel Zone retreat pairs pale interiors and Caribbean frontage with an unusually generous all-inclusive package: À la carte dining, premium drinks, 24-hour room service, and access to the spa’s hydrotherapy circuit are all included. Perched on the tip of Punta Cancún, Hyatt Ziva makes the most of its peninsula setting, with room for both family playtime and grown-up downtime. Little ones can race down waterslides and splash beneath fountains, while teenagers claim their own turf over billiards and foosball in the teens' lounge. items.title: 7 Best Hotels in Antigua, the Caribbean Island With a Beach for Every Day of the Year
items.summary: From ultra-luxe five-star resorts to boutique beach hideaways, these are the properties worth booking in Antigua.
items.text: Central America and the Caribbean Chevron Antigua Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story With endless white-sand beaches , acres of rugged rainforest, and plenty of untouched tangle just waiting to be explored, the best hotels in Antigua celebrate its landscape, which remains largely true to how nature intended. Most of the properties on this glorious Caribbean island are a stone’s throw from the crystal-clear waters that lap its powder-soft shores. It’s a beach-lover’s dream, and anyone visiting would be hard-pressed to see every stretch of golden sand—as the saying goes, there’s “a beach for every day of the year” here (yes, an even 365). Visit between June and October , and you might just be lucky enough to watch baby turtles emerging blurry-eyed from their shells before scuttling to the sea. There are optimal times for surfing here, too, but the year-round promise is that the vibe on this island is chill. Days stretch lazily from sunrise swims to rum-fueled sundowners, with the opportunity for a poolside snooze in between. It’s easy to sink into vacation mode here, especially when you’re checking into one of the best hotels in Antigua. We've rounded up the most luxurious options on the island below, from high-end resorts with all the frills to boutique hideaways so good you’ll be booking your return before you’ve even left for home. items.title: 8 Dreamy Hotels Our NYC Editors Are Booking This Winter
items.summary: Because sometimes all you need is a quick change of scenery to tackle the winter blues.
items.text: Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story If there’s one thing the editors at Condé Nast Traveler love, it’s weekendmaxxing . We’re all about scouting the very best hotels upstate , or catching a quick flight to Miami, all before returning back to our New York City office by Monday. The art of the weekend trip becomes especially important in the wintertime, when the city closes its blinds and hibernates until spring. This is when an off-season jaunt to the Rockaways, or a hideaway in a Berkshires lodge, becomes all the more appealing. Essentially, we love a trip where you can get cozy somewhere else—because sometimes all you need is a simple change of scenery to tackle the winter blues. From wellness sanctuaries nestled in the Catskills to country retreats in New England , these are the hotels our editors are eyeing for when the weather turns brisk, all within a few hours of NYC or a short flight away. Courtesy Auberge Collection Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Courtesy Auberge Collection Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Courtesy Auberge Collection Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Courtesy Auberge Collection Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Chevron Chevron Mayflower Inn & Spa, Auberge Collection Readers' Choice Readers' Choice Awards 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 Hannah Chubb , senior commerce editor Where are you staying? Mayflower Inn & Spa, Washington, Connecticut What drew you to this hotel? I visited Mayflower Inn back in spring 2024 with one of my best friends while she was pregnant with her second baby, and I’ve been dying to go back ever since. I don’t know if I’ve ever felt more relaxed than I did while there—we spent hours in the spa, chatted by the firepits, stuffed ourselves with farm-fresh meals, and feasted our eyes on some incredible interior design. What are you eating? I won’t be leaving the hotel for food, that’s for sure. I’m always impressed by the F&B at Auberge properties, and the Mayflower Inn was no exception. The Garden Room offers creative but approachable seasonal cuisine from breakfast through dinner (don’t skip the burger), and the Tap Room is where you’ll find a tavern-style food menu plus a mixologist slinging delicious cocktails and mocktails. What do you hope to get up to in the area? The Mayflower Inn is located in Washington, Connecticut, a small town in Litchfield County , a region beloved by many of my colleagues. Next time I visit the hotel, I’ll have to make a few stops along the way to see what all the fuss is about. Urban Cowboy Lodge has been on my weekend getaway wish list for years, and there’s something about it in winter that feels particularly charming—maybe it’s the delightful snow-filled view from the bathtub (pictured above) that drew me in. I’m imagining myself curled up with a good book by the lounge’s fireplace, draped in a Pendleton blanket, then dipping into the aforementioned copper clawfoot bathtubs. At just about two-and-a-half hours north of Manhattan, it’s a not-too-far excursion I’m saving for when I really need a break from winter in the city. What are you eating? Phoenicia Diner , of course. I’m also keen to try out some of the many craft beers at Ralph’s Bar. What do you hope to get up to in the area? I’m not a skier, so in the winter, heading to the Catskills comes with more of a stay-indoors-and-get-cozy vibe for me. Besides a pit stop at Phoenicia Diner, I imagine the furthest I’ll trek is over to the sauna and bowling alley. Aside from the ocean views—poetically perfect for New York in the winter—The Rockaway is home to one of my favorite wellness scenes in the city . The space transforms its outdoor pool area (which, in the summer months, is home to outdoor concerts and DJ-led pool parties) into the cozy Winter Pool House . The space gets decked out with outdoor cedar barrel saunas and the softest plush robes to wear while you transition to the heated outdoor pool. The warm water mixed with the ice-cold breeze coming off the nearby coastline is glorious. What are you eating? I’ll be heading to Margie’s—the mood-lit hotel lobby restaurant—and ordering a juicy cheeseburger and a frosty gin martini. What better way to warm your soul? What do you hope to get up to in the area? The beauty of visiting this hotel in winter? No summer beach crowds. items.title: Where to Eat Gluten-Free in Montreal
items.summary: Travel and food writer Luke Pyenson shares where to find the city’s best gluten-free bites, sips, and dining experiences.
items.text: Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Recently I’ve noticed more and more food people going to Montreal —and who can blame them? This laid-back bilingual gem on the St. Lawrence River is one of North America’s very best food cities. Personally I’ve loved it since my first visit almost 20 years ago. Montreal’s wonderful food scene draws me back year after year, sometimes multiple times,and by now the six-hour drive from my home in New York City feels like a breeze. It helps to know that my top meals of the year are waiting just across the border. But for the past two years, following my wife’s celiac diagnosis, I have been navigating the city a little differently. When I was younger, trips to Montreal meant poutine, bagels, smoked-meat sandwiches, and a plethora of other canonical Québécois favorites that happen to be full of gluten. These days we prioritize other local favorites and have developed a dependable roster of businesses we trust—and that don’t feel like a compromise. Luckily there are a ton of them; we’ve been thrilled to discover that Montreal is a paradise for gluten-free eating. Boulangerie Le Marquis Dedicated bakery scene In my opinion the only gluten-free Montreal-style bagels worth sampling are located in Burlington, Vermont. But Montreal is a city that takes its baked goods seriously, and it’s home to a handful of excellent dedicated gluten-free bakeries. You will not miss the bagels. Instead how about a croissant? Any gluten-free eater knows croissants are one of the hardest pastries to get right without gluten. As a rule my wife and I don’t really bother—unless we’re in Montreal. At Boulangerie Le Marquis , near Jean-Talon Market, and sister business Le Marquis Signature Santé , in Old Montreal, magnificent pains au chocolat and gluten-free croissants—available in plain, almond, and chocolate-almond varieties—arrive hot out of the oven all morning long. Flaky laminated pastry is a near-impossible feat in the gluten-free world, but Le Marquis has perfected it. We favor the pains au chocolat and almond croissants, but it’s tough to go wrong. Even more unique is the gluten-free manouché at La Bolo à Lolo , a GF market and takeaway in the Plateau. Chef and owner Gordy Moufarrej emigrated from Lebanon to Montreal as a boy and uses his mother’s homemade za’atar in these addictive flatbreads. Made from Moufarrej’s proprietary GF flour blend, they are topped with a paste of olive oil and za’atar, plus cheese if you want (you do). A number of sandwiches made with the same base are available, but we’ve never gotten past the manouché—on our last visit to Montreal, we went three days in a row. A sweet galette from Crêperie du Marché Luke Pyenson Perhaps unsurprisingly for a French-speaking city, crepes are another great option, and Montreal boasts an amazing spot for 100% buckwheat Breton-style galettes. At Crêperie du Marché , a bustling stall at Jean-Talon Market, cooks turn out a dedicated gluten-free menu of lacy galettes with both savory and sweet fillings. It’s a personal choice, but we like the cheeky selections that mix both: ham, cheese, eggs, potatoes, and a drizzle of maple syrup. Why not? Nearby is cheery, quirky Cantine Panella , a dedicated gluten-free bakery and café run by the Peruvian chef Alessandra Perona. Her South American sensibility means breads are made with flours like quinoa, cassava, and sweet potato, which gives them a delightful chewiness. We like to stock up on a few of these to bring home, though they sometimes don’t last the drive. Chicken Of all Montreal’s classic foods, rotisserie chicken might be my favorite. At Québécois-style rotisseries it’s slow-roasted on a spit and accompanied by gravy; at Portuguese spots it’s often spatchcocked and grilled over charcoal, then served with piri-piri sauce. In both cases gluten sometimes spoils the fun: Traditional establishments like the legendary Chalet Bar-B-Q and Portuguese eatery Ma Poule Mouillée both use wheat flour in their sauces. No matter—these are far from your only options. Piri-Piri Chicken at Rôtisserie Coco Rico Luke Pyenson At Rôtisserie Coco Rico , a Plateau institution open since 1970, the chicken is spit-roasted and served with GF piri-piri in a mélange of the two dominant local styles. On the side fries from a dedicated GF fryer are among the city’s best (and this is a city with great french fries), but don’t sleep on the roasted potatoes, full of savory chicken flavor. More refined, and representing the French Canadian tradition, is Little Italy’s Rôtisserie La Lune , from the team behind überpopular restaurant and wine bar Mon Lapin. Gorgeous, plump birds are served with rich gluten-free gravy and excellent fries that come from a blessedly dedicated fryer. The same fryer is also responsible for the unbelievable Croqu’Ailes Farcies XL, which are deboned chicken wings stuffed with more chicken and deep-fried. Every meal here should start with these. But the kitchen has an equally deft hand with seasonal salads and veggie-focused sides—almost always gluten-free and an essential counterweight on the table. Courtesy Mon Lapin Wine bars and neo-bistros Down the street from La Lune, Mon Lapin is equally adept at catering to gluten-free diners: On two recent visits most of the menu was in play. Dishes change with the seasons, but friendly servers will guide your choices (and help you navigate the impressive wine list). Make sure to save room for the restaurant’s signature buckwheat layer cake, accented with buckwheat honey caramel, fromage blanc, and crisp shards of buckwheat tuile. I’m not sure there’s a better gluten-free dessert on the continent. Mon Lapin’s co-owners, chefs Jessica Noël and Marc-Olivier Frappier, and wine director Vanya Filipovic, are all alums of the trendsetting Little Burgundy eatery and wine bar Vin Papillon , whose chef and owner happens to be celiac. Best known as half of the duo that opened Montreal icon Joe Beef , Fred Morin now presides over thos

items.text: UCHIKO MIAMI - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE Uchiko blends tropical brutalism with Japanese deco influences, creating a space that feels both rooted in its marina-side setting and like an enchanting escape. The design celebrates contrasts—raw and refined, bold and intimate—where handcrafted details, textured materials, and vibrant colors transport guests into a world of beauty and wonder. UCHIKO MIAMI UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Miami, FL ROLE Interior Design YEAR 2025 partners Hai Hospitality City Construction Pineapple Procurement Form Group AE Design William Jess Laird SELECTED PRESS Uchiko is a poetic interpretation of Miami Beach’s spirit, blending tropical brutalism with the elegance of Japanese deco influences to create a space that feels like an escape, yet remains deeply rooted in its marina-side setting. It is a celebration of contrasts—raw and refined, bold and intimate, coastal and cosmopolitan—designed to transport guests to a world of beauty and wonder. The design of Uchiko embraces hand-crafted elements and a palette of highly textured materials and celebrates the beauty of imperfection. The material palette tells a story of the marina and its textures. Exposed concrete, softened by hand-pressed stone and shell accents, echoes the coast’s rocks where sea life finds refuge, while rich teak wood shutters add warmth and a sense of grounded elegance and tropicalism. At the entrance, the host stand is inspired by Japanese thatched roofs—setting the tone with an inviting and handcrafted feel. At the heart of the space is the signature glass block bar, a glowing jewel that captures the light of the setting sun and casts rippling reflections onto the ceiling, evoking the magic of water at golden hour. This luminous centerpiece anchors the dining room, creating an enchanting ambiance that shifts with the light as the sun sets. The color palette is a love letter to the marina’s depths, with gradients of deep blues blending seamlessly into the space. Bursts of vibrancy appear in playful artwork depicting oceanic ingredients used in the cuisine, while sea green marble mosaics are found accented in the concrete floors throughout for a modern touch. These details, paired with lush tropical plantings, bring an organic softness to the design, imbuing the space with life and vitality. The private dining room is a sanctuary within a sanctuary, an intimate retreat framed by Japanese-inspired sliding drapery and featuring a dramatic carved stone fireplace. With its moody lighting, rich textures, and enveloping warmth, the room feels like a hidden world filled with artful discoveries. Additional Japanese influences are woven throughout, from the handcrafted copper light fixtures and intricate deco-inspired drink rails to the tiled bathrooms, where rich aubergine-colored tiles immerse you in a moment of unexpected indulgence. Every element of the design feels as though it could exist nowhere else, from the tactile materials to the thoughtful craftsmanship. Uchiko embodies the essence of its setting: vibrant, layered, and timeless. It is not merely a place to dine—it is a journey through light and texture, history and innovation, sea and sky. The result is a space that invites guests to linger, discover, and connect. Whether basking in the golden glow of the bar or marveling at the interplay of textures, Uchiko leaves an indelible impression—an elevated experience that feels both effortless and extraordinary. items.title: THE TUSK BAR & BRASS - Islyn
items.text: THE TUSK BAR & BRASS - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE Through the Art Deco lobby of The Evelyn hotel, is The Tusk Bar, a cocktail and oyster bar that was recently named one of Esquire’s Best Bars in America, 2024. The glamorous bar room marries the spirit of the roaring 20s with the convivial attitude of mid-century cocktail parties, sharing the timelessness of a warm welcome, a well-made drink, a freshly shucked oyster - and a good time. Through the bar you'll find Brass, a new destination restaurant that pays homage to the grand dining rooms of New York. Taking inspiration from the style of French brasseries but without adhering to their playbook, Brass showcases the playful contemporary spirit that characterize chefs Jeremiah Stone and Fabian Von Hauske Valtierra’s cuisine. THE TUSK BAR & BRASS UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION New York, NY ROLE Interior Design YEAR 2024 partners Nick Hatsatouris and Lincoln Pilcher Jeremiah Stone and Fabián von Hauske Valtierra AE Design Wagner Hamill Inc David Dignam SELECTED PRESS NYT’S Esquire Tucked away within the Evelyn Hotel, a historic Art Deco building built in 1903, on the storied stretch of Tin Pan Alley, the evening begins at The Tusk Bar. Stepping inside feels like entering a Parisian apartment of the 1920s—timeless, intimate, and effortlessly elegant. The glow of warm light bounces off marble surfaces, plush seating beckons, and the air hums with an unhurried energy. A vintage taxidermy ostrich stands watch over the bar’s graceful dining room, where expertly crafted cocktails are poured with precision and care. Here, time slows. The first sip is a quiet indulgence, an invitation to unwind. The menu is an elegant balance of classic technique and modern ingenuity created by chefs Jeremiah Stone and Fabián von Hauske Valtierra. Oysters arrive on ice, briny and cold, the perfect prelude to an evening that is just beginning. When the moment feels right, guests make their way through the hotel and into the grand dining room of Brass, where the golden age of New York meets the bold spirit of French New Wave cinema and guests can enjoy “two-sipper cocktails” featuring original drinks and some New Orleans classics like a mini French 75 or an ice cold sazerac, before their meal begins. The space is lush with rich colors—muted green walls, jewel-toned seating, and accents of walnut and original mosaic marble floors, all illuminated beneath a restored skylight. At the center, a grand piano casts a sense of theater over the room, setting the stage for an evening of indulgence. The soft glow of tobacco-hued chandeliers flickers against oversized mirrors, reflecting laughter and candlelight, creating a world that is both sultry and alive. At Brass, the chefs reinvent the classic brasserie with a modern perspective. The menu includes rich dishes such as crab and maitake mushroom tartlet, ricotta gnudi, and mains like duck breast, pork shoulder, and a wagyu steak that slices like butter. Seated beneath the warm amber glow, dinner unfolds in courses, each dish a careful balance of decadence and restraint. Conversations stretch between bites, weaving through the air like music. For those seeking a more intimate setting, the private dining room offers a retreat wrapped in deep plum hues, velvet drapes, and brass details—an opulent hideaway that feels like a backstage secret, tucked away from the energy of the main room. The crab and maitake mushroom tartlet is both earthy and rich, while ricotta gnudi melts effortlessly on the tongue. Spaces DISCIPLINES | Spaces Spatial Awareness Our strength lies in shaping the feel and function of a space long before material choices come into play, allowing design elements to follow with intention and clarity. what we do Spatial Audit & Planning Programming Evaluation & Development Concept Development Furniture and Finish Plans Schematic Designs Design Development Construction Design Guidelines Feeling Before Seeing ‍ Our designs never begin with a fixed idea. The foundation lies in understanding the emotional experience a space should evoke and shaping it to carry that vision while navigating real-world design constraints. North Star ‍ For over 45 years, we have designed experiences through the spaces we create, guided by the belief that every project begins with a client’s narrative. Using insights we gather, our teams shape journeys defined by emotional touchpoints, reinforcing brand positioning and guiding every design decision. Tandem Design ‍ As a creative design studio, we work in tandem with interiors, art, product, and planning to ensure that every element supports a unified narrative. Working in this way ensures cohesion, allowing small details to become integral to a space and design rather than just an add on. Light, art, and signage merge seamlessly to enhance the spatial narrative. Place Making ‍ While we operate from studios in Toronto and New York, our work is international, giving us lived and project experience needed to anchor each design within its context. Our long list of global collaborations and local insights allows us to introduce thoughtful references that feel genuine and grounded in place. Network Effect ‍ As we continue into our fifth decade, we maintain relationships with clients and partners forged in our earliest work. The trust and creative partnerships built over time give our teams shared understanding and access to insights that guide each project. Even when challenges arise, the foundations we've built help to navigate projects with clarity and ease. Drag Click to play What we've Done The Palace Muli Showroom Beijing Honoring Emotions MULI’s Beijing flagship sits within a heritage shell of significant presence. The challenge was to honor the architecture’s weight while shaping a contemporary experience that slows a visitor and centers emotion before product. Grounded Relevance The project required creating a calm counterpoint to the space’s historic intensity. We shaped the interior around a feeling-before-seeing rhythm, using softened thresholds, gentle turns and curated sightlines that invite reflection rather than rush. The narrative centered on attentiveness and materials that quiet the senses through stone and metal in muted finishes that absorb rather than broadcast. Working across lighting, styling, and planning, we introduced subtle gestures that guide attention, resulting in a store where heritage and modernity meet through experience rather than ornament. AMAN Residences Tokyo Connected Sanctuary The Aman Residences asked us to translate the brand’s resort calm into private homes atop the Mori JP Tower. The challenge was to create a space that feels serene, grounded, and unmistakably residential while maintaining the DNA of Aman. Living Calm We designed the Aman Residences as a gradual transition from Tokyo’s urban intensity into sky-level quiet, guided by Japanese principles of restraint and intentional pacing. Long sightlines, softened corners, and calibrated thresholds establish calm, while tactile woods, subtle handwork, shadow-holding stone, and precise joinery root the residences in craft rather than motif and give them a grounded local character. Supported by every discipline working in tandem and by our longstanding relationship with Aman, the brand’s essence shapes daily living in a serene and deeply human way. Raffles Sentosa He

items.title: Beauty in Function
items.text: Beauty in Function Products Beauty in Function Our product design team works to strike a balance between the emotional and the practical. what we do Bespoke Furniture product strategy Exhibition Design & Curation Works Well With Others ‍ We design products that belong. Our interior design foundation means every piece complements the room, not just the brief. It's an approach that draws from a deep understanding of context, from the interplay of form and function to cultural insights gained through projects around the world. This perspective allows us to create designs that resonate across places and people. Emotionally centered ‍ We build function into emotionally engaging objects. We always begin with the feeling we want to create and the result is work with a presence that doesn't wear out. Relationship inspired ‍ Great design comes from trust, clarity, and momentum. We collaborate closely to align vision, constraints, and craft. Without a type ‍ From furniture to architectural finishes, accessories and textiles, our work is united by curiosity and partners who welcome fresh thinking. Drag Click to play What we've Done Molteni & C Going With the Flow Surf was born from a Carlo Molteni's challenge. “If you think you’re good, design a sofa.” The Surf sofa evolved over five years into a piece shaped by curiosity, context, and the pursuit of a sectional that feels more fluid than modular. “You know, this is so beautiful and unique from every angle.” A lot of sofas look generic from the back. Of course, then he asked Vincent Van Duysen, the creative director of Molteni, what he thought, and Van Duysen said, “It’s nice, but it’s not Molteni.” But Carlo Molteni said, “I’m doing it anyway.” - Glenn Pushelberg A Softer Kind of Modularity Surf began not with a concept of modularity, but with the feeling of fluid motion. Instead of the rigid geometry typical of sectional systems, we looked to the motion of water and waves, shaping a form that flows in every direction. Working closely with Molteni & C, we sketched, carved, stretched fabric, and engineered side by side to explore both potential and constraint. The result is a modular system that behaves with flexibility but appears as a singular, sculptural gesture—comfortable, calm, and quietly confident in any space. Tribù Understated, Engineered, Enduring Our partnership with Tribu is defined by shared values—restraint, precision, sustainability, and a commitment to pushing outdoor furniture beyond expectation. Together, we explore how clarity in design can balance craftsmanship with environmental responsibility. ‍ A Design Language Grown Together The collaboration with Tribu began with a shared respect for subtlety that grew into a partnership spanning four collections. Each piece was shaped in context, considering how it lives within architecture, landscape, and daily routines, resulting in collections that feel light, quiet, and deeply considered. Balancing expressive form with Tribu's engineering precision opened new possibilities: the suspended bridge dynamism of Nodi, the cocooned softness of Elio, and the indoor outdoor fluidity of Amanu. Designed to mix across collections, each piece contributes to a cohesive story, while reinforcing a shared belief that simplicity, executed with rigor, can be transformative. Moxy Hotel Times sqaure A System Built for Small Spaces With Big Personalities Moxy Times Square redefined the North American micro-hotel concept, and the product collection set the benchmark across forty properties, establishing a new standard for compact hospitality.‍ Adaptable by Design We approached the collection as a toolkit shaped by the realities of compact living, with foldable pieces, integrated storage, and multi-use furniture that combine the ingenuity of urban camping with the spatial discipline of traditional ryokans. items.title: Evoking experience
items.text: Evoking experience Art Evoking experience Art is not a decorative final flourish for us. It is essential to storytelling, spatial harmony, and in creating an emotional connection and attraction to a project. what we do Services in Partnership with Hanabi Art Budget development Art procurement Artist Management Commissioned artwork Production schedules & timelines Crating and shipping Instillation oversight Art as a Narrative Element ‍ Rather than treating art as only a visual element, we weave it into the overall design concept from the outset helping reinforce a narrative and giving people moments to remember. Art as a Holder Of Place ‍ Culture is a response to place. In the pursuit of global appeal, many designs fail to recognize that a contemporary interpretation of local context, rather than a sanitized international perspective, is what connects a project to culture and gives it the authenticity that resonates with people both near and far. Architectural Integration ‍ Art can move beyond traditional mediums, using light, sculpture, and texture to create intimate or monumental moments that invite reflection or guide you along a path. Immersive Installations ‍ Texture, placement, and scale transform art from something to be admired into something to be experienced. Subtle, Yet Provocative Art Choices ‍ We avoid overt statements, favoring subtle interventions that invite curiosity and discovery. ‍ Drag Click to play What we've Done Centurion Lounge New York Art Sets Centurion Apart Known for its smart airport lounges, American Express sought to evolve into a true private members club within urban locations. Art became a key element to the experience, helping attract clients away from traditional competitors. A Salonniere's New York Drawing inspiration from the New York, the salon celebrates the city’s vibrant art scene and its legacy as a dynamic hub of creativity and cultural exchange. We imagined the spaces as a contemporary interpretation of a modern day salonnière’s home, a gathering place where art, culture, and conversation come together. The art collection features a mix of established and emerging artists, across different mediums, and styles, all rooted in New York as their point of origin and influence. Featured Artist: Diane Arbus, Nan Golden, Bill Cunningham, Ruth Orkin, Dennis Lin, Jason Boyd Kinsella, Vivian Maier, Tseng Kwong Chi Raffles Hotel Sentosa Bridging Urban to Oasis Our challenge was to connect the new development to the original hotel built in1887 across the harbor, while navigating the atmospheric differences between the storied urban hotel and the new resort typologies. Hanabi: Art And Artists curated and provided all artwork in the public areas and guest villas, reinforcing the Raffles tradition of subtly linking past and present through art. Connecting to Context The unifying concept for art in this project was to extend the natural world into the built environment, blurring the lines between indoors and outdoors. The goal was to offer guests moments to pause, wonder, and reflect, much like nature itself. Through a range of artistic techniques and perspectives, we showcase nature’s diversity. Each piece presents a distinct interpretation of the serenity found in the natural world, from realistic depictions to abstract forms. Featured Artist: André Wee, Ryan Loi ‍ Moxy Hotel Downtown Los Angeles Escaping the Obvious The Moxy brand is provocative, irreverent, and a bit reckless. Those who choose to stay downtown lean into California’s dark and stormy side rather than its sun and palm trees. We reimagined California through the eyes of a modern desert nomad setting out on their own adventure, discovering the unexpected during their stay Art that Adds Dimension Theart curation invites guests into a state of mind that encourages curiosity sense of adventure. items.title: Light as a Defining element
items.text: Light as a Defining element Lighting Light as a Defining element Light is the only element that can transform a space in an instant. It can move you emotionally or guide you through a journey by illuminating a path. what we do Conceptual Design Requirement Development Lighting Studies and Photometric Calculations Schematic Layouts Luminaire & Control System Specification Custom Development for Architectural Integration Coordination & Review of Mockups Construction Administration On-site Equipment Focusing & System Programming Brand Lighting Design Guidelines Refresh/Upgrade Project Program Emotional Requirements ‍ Our strength lies in meeting functional requirements while delivering an emotional impact going beyond the measure of light. Our concepts are grounded in a narrative that reflects a client’s identity, creating moments of drama, tranquility, sensuality, and clarity throughout a guest's journey. Relational Research ‍ We bring together insights from international projects with in-depth research into local contexts and project specific requirements. Our core strength is transforming a design vision into reality, navigating a complex network of global requirements. Tandem Design ‍ As a creative design studio, we collaborate across interiors, art, wayfinding, product, and planning so that the resulting scheme becomes a seamless part of the narrative. Through this process, light guides the design and becomes an integral feature rather than an after thought. Visual Language ‍ Through documentation, the lighting scheme is developed and refined. Spaces are visualized in three dimensions for both day and night, culminating in a comprehensive drawing package that includes lighting control specifications, renderings, and all required plans and elevations. ‍ Realizing The Vision ‍ In-house models, study mockups, and sample reviews are part of our process and help us understand how light performs, reflects, and refracts. We study floor plans, elevations, key design moments to test applications of the lighting scheme. This process allows us to validate the design intent or strategy and refine its final implementation. On-Site Calibration ‍ The process reveals its true artistry when each space is crafted by hand. Even the smallest adjustment, such as a subtle shift in a recessed angle, can have a significant impact on the experience. ‍ Drag Click to play What we've Done The Pinky Ring Las Vegas Showmanship Bruno Mars envisioned a cocktail lounge and live music venue at the Bellagio Hotel and Casino as an opulent adult playground, where the atmosphere of luxury could be seen, felt, and lived. The Pinky Ring immerses guests in an alluring atmosphere reminiscent of a 1970s private penthouse party. Our task was to create a dramatic environment without relying on cliché notions of Vegas opulence. Perpetual Allure Through a strategic interplay of low-level, contrast, and accent lighting, we set out to create a space where people both look and feel their best. Lighting the façade was designed to highlight the venue within the broader casino floor while maintaining the privacy expected of a VIP experience. Illumination at the Grammy wall in the hall leading into the Pinky Ring presented a particular challenge. The team focused on finding the right compact fixture to fit within the smaller alcove yet powerful enough to light the Grammys effectively. On the main floor, lighting was kept warm and inviting, with special attention placed on the bar and stage areas. A coordinated DMX system enables lighting to adapt fluidly to different moods and functions, from stage performances to lounge, disco, and dance settings. The increased complexity of the stage design called for close coordination with lighting specialists to develop and integrate the appropriate systems. Styling DISCIPLINES | Styling Imbuing Authenticity When used thoughtfully, art, objects, and accessories establish a connection to place and evoke intimacy at a human scale. Each narrative explores the archetypes and muses that shape a project, the items they curate, and how they move and live within the space. Object Agnostic ‍ Our concepts move beyond the obvious, incorporating layered accessories, florals, materials, and color schemes. Each element contributes to a cohesive and fluid narrative. Cultural Connection ‍ Our projects feature custom commissions from local and national artists that connect residents and travelers to their surroundings. Our deep network and long-standing relationships provide access to exclusive pieces and collaborations, ensuring each work feels authentic and grounded, even when sparked by a single idea. Not Lost in Translation ‍ Projects where clients work closely with us on-site often yield the strongest results. We source alongside clients and act as the conduit between their vision and artisans who may hesitate to engage independently. Our role as translator, bridging their goals and the nuanced process of craft and creation, is what defines our value. Applied Arts ‍ The Styling team’s core strength lies in realizing a unique vision. We reference precedent projects, helping clarify intentions and demonstrate the value of strategic investment. Our deep experience and long-standing relationships allow us to translate digital concepts into physical form, guiding each project through prototyping, production, and on-site adaptation to achieve its final result. Drag Click to play What we've Done Aman Residences Tokyo Connecting Ground to Air Our clients, the Aman Group and Mori Building Co., envisioned both a literal and figurative crown for the top of the Mori JP Tower, the tallest building in Japan. Perched at the peak, the residences remain connected to the vibrant village below—a community centered on connectivity, culture, and nature. Client Collaboration Our styling team led the narrative development, research, and sourcing through to on-site installation. The client recognized styling as an essential element, collaborating with us and their procurement team to source unique artifacts and commission custom pieces from our network of Japanese artisans. The result is communal spaces shaped with clarity and purpose, each carrying a character of its own. Moxy Hotel Downtown Los Angeles Take Two Bold choices, curiosity, and a sense of adventure shaped the styling for Moxy DTLA, capturing the brand’s playful spirit. Inspired by a desire to reimagine the neighborhood through a fresh and contemporary lens, we developed a narrative that gives the space its own character. As a two brand hotel tower, Moxy needed to establish its own identity while maintaining a clear relationship to AC DTLA, achieving balance without separation. Desert Rose The styling concept built on the narrative of an adventurous muse journeying across the California desert on their motorcycle. items.title: Narrative to Imperative
items.text: Narrative to Imperative Branding & Wayfinding Narrative to Imperative Developing a brand from the macro concept down to the micro details of directional wayfinding allows us to craft a cohesive story, punctuated with moments that guide guests through each experience with ease. what we do Brand Concept Development Brand & Project Positioning Identity Development Touchpoint Design & Rollout Guidelines User Journey Mapping Information Design Environmental Graphic Design Physical and Digital Signage & Wayfinding Material & Production Advisory SWOT Team ‍ Before design begins, we move beyond physical and stylistic requirements, conducting competitive and client analysis to identify opportunities and define the negative space that allow each project to stand out. North Star ‍ For over 45 years, we have designed experiences through interiors, guided by the belief that impactful design begins with a client’s narrative. Using the insights we gather, we shape journeys defined by emotional touch points that reinforce brand positioning and guide every design decision. ‍ Tandem Design ‍ As a creative design studio, we work in tandem with interiors, art, product, and planning so that every element supports a unified narrative. Through this process, cohesion is achieved, allowing small wayfinding details to guide the design and become integral rather than added-on. Light, art, and signage merge seamlessly to enhance the spatial narrative. ‍ Visual Language ‍ We create tools that help internal and external teams carry the vision forward and maintain design integrity. We then establish a clear standard and a project framework that guides decision making as the project evolves. ‍ Drag Click to play What we've Done Park Villa Residence Manila Blank Slate We began the project with extensive market research into what defines ultra-luxury residences around the world, gaining a deeper understanding of design and guest experience at this level. Building on these insights, we developed a brand strategy and positioning to help the client define how this project in Manila should be presented and promoted. Services: Brand positioning, Wayfinding, Information Design ‍ Moxy Hotel Downtown Los Angeles Guided by Subtle Cues For this project, we designed both the room numbers and the corridor carpet pattern. The overall concept was inspired by the idea of being on the road and the experience of travel. Drawing references from LAX, we looked at how airports use lines and signage systems to guide pilots through space. Translating that into the interior, we created carpet patterns that subtly lead guests along the corridors without relying on wall signage. The room numbers were designed with a nod to old-school flipping signs once found in train stations and airports, adding a layer of nostalgia to the journey. Services: Wayfinding ‍ Ami Woodear Hong Kong Distinct Characters We were tasked with naming and developing the identity for this project: a French-style cuisine restaurant paired with a bar featuring one of the rarest whisky collections in Hong Kong. The restaurant was named Ami—French for ‘friends’—to evoke warmth, connection, and the spirit of friendship. The bar was named Woodear , inspired by the unique mushroom that thrives in dark, earthy forests, reflecting the interiors’ moody, forest-like palette. The design challenge was to give each venue its own distinct identity while ensuring they still felt connected. Our solution blended both brands through subtle overlaps—such as a business card split down the middle—allowing them to standalone or work together as a unified whole. items.title: Made Blue Foundation | Lore Group | Sustainable Hospitality
items.text: Made Blue Foundation We have joined forces with the Made Blue Foundation so that when you stay in our hotels, you can sleep (and shower) easier knowing that you're helping providing water where it’s most needed, from Asia and Africa to the Americas. Meet Made Blue Who are Made Blue? This entrepreneurial-minded water charity is on a mission to provide everyone with access to clean drinking water. Water stress and scarcity is a threat that’s long been listed with rising temperatures as a Global Risk by the World Economic Forum — few understand this better than this non-profit founded in the Netherlands in 2014. How do we work together? Our partnership funds 100 litres of clean, fresh water for every room night sold. Guests across each of the our seven hotels are given this ‘gift’ to pay forward — an amount funded, in its entirety, by Lore. Every guest has the power to decide where, and whom, the total amount made possible by their stay will support: each occupied night provides one full day of clean water for a household in Bangalore to Mexico City, as delivered by Made Blue Foundation. 100 million litres of clean drinking water Together with our guests, we have helped deliver 100 million litres of clean drinking water through our partnership with Made Blue Foundation. This milestone belongs to every guest who has stayed with us. To find out more about the Made Blue Foundation, and the projects and people who benefit from Lore Group's gift of clean water - please either visit the foundation's website below, or get in touch with us directly.
